Oh dear! she sighed to herself as she sat in a gloomy corner of the dimly lit room. She stared blankly at the wall in front of her, with no hope or excitement in her eyes. She softly muttered to herself, Oh my god, literally no one can understand what I'm going through right now.

This moment of dread was suddenly disrupted, like a jolt of electricity, when her coworkers barged into the office and turned on the bright lights. Hey, what’s up? Why are you sitting here looking all somber? they asked. But before she could answer, they swiftly moved on to discussing their project deadline. It was as if no one cared. What the hell, she thought to herself.

As she sat there with her shoulders hunched and a distressing look on her face, the conversations around her echoed in her ears. Her boss, as usual, walked into the room with his perpetual irritated scowl and said in a stern voice, Guys, come on, get to work. We need to meet this deadline. Everyone hurriedly ran to their desks and pretended to get to work, all while assuming nothing was seriously wrong with her.

Seeing everyone looking alert and productive, the boss turned his gaze towards her. Sarah, stop looking so dreadful, he said. I just realized something. Sarah’s ears perked up and her shoulders straightened. What, boss? What did you realize? she asked.

The boss said, Sarah, you’re not dreading anything! In fact, you’re literally enjoying life right now.

This took Sarah aback, and she instantly protested. Come on. No, I am totally not enjoying life right now.

The boss smirked. Sarah, you know we know you. And you know that we can tell when you are dreading something, right? And today, we know you are totally not dreading life.

Hearing this, Sarah couldn’t help but smirk a little. She coyly said, No, I am so not okay.

Before she could continue, one of her bosses jumped in. Sarah, you’re literally grumpy every day, but today we noticed that you are not. By brooding now, you are literally trying to keep up with your everyday persona. Jeez, Sarah, let loose a bit and accept that today is not a gloomy day and you are going to have fun.

This made Sarah chuckle, which turned into a burst of laughter. She sheepishly admitted, Yeah, fine. I am literally pretending right now. Nothing’s got me dreading anything. You’re right, I was trying to keep up with my everyday persona.

The room echoed with laughter, and someone in the background said, Silly Sarah. They all got back to work with grins on their faces.
